title: Henry Laurens (Nantes) → James Bourdieu (London): clear letter with 13 numerical code designations (12 distinct numbers), key not known
shelfmark: University of South Carolina, South Caroliniana Library, Henry Laurens Papers (accession 13612), amerrevsc id 2206 (images 2203-2205)
folio_note: Three pages, images 2203 to 2205 of record 2206. 13 code positions, 12 distinct numbers (only 19 repeats), in this order: 29 (page 1, line 10); 21, 19, 55, 57, 68, 36, 54, 23, 56, 19, 67, 20 (page 2, lines 11 to 21); none on page 3. The rest is clear English. Two AI readers working without a key agree on all 13.
status: Not on DECODE (keyword search 'Bourdieu': 0 records, 20 Nov 2026); not in the catalogue or the leads (known.py 'Bourdieu', '13612', 'amerrevsc', 'Laurens': only the research note itself and lead 1435, a different letter of 1778). The Papers of Henry Laurens, vol. 15 (1999), seen in Google Books snippets, say the key to the Laurens-Bourdieu number code is not known and that the numbers do not seem to have been fixed to persons; the volume prints the letter of 4 June 1782 (pp. 526-528) and, by the contributor's reading of its index, not this letter in full. What the research note research/laurens_bourdieu_1782/ (PR #827) adds: here Laurens quotes what he wrote to Franklin on 7 Aug 1782 (postscript, image 2497) with numbers for the names, so 68 = Mr Bourdieu, 36 = American Independence, 54 = Lord S (Shelburne, per the Laurens editors) and 23 = the French interest (exact word unknown). Two looser comparisons put Franklin at both 19s (Laurens to Oswald, 7 Aug, image 2495; 'neither 56 nor 19' against the postscript's 'neither Count Vergennes nor yourself'), as the edition had suggested for June; 56 = Vergennes is suggested and left open. Six of 13 positions have a referent; three of them (68, 36, 54) rest on a word-for-word parallel. Open: 29, 21, 55, 57, 56, 67, 20. The letter to Bourdieu of 28 Aug 1782 (image 2460) repeats 19 and 68 ('I have lately heard from 19. Seemingly a studied silence respecting the concerns of 68') and has 'No. 45'; Franklin and Bourdieu fit there, which is compatibility, not confirmation. The letter of 30 Nov 1782 (image 2994) has 44, open. A pre-registered check of six letters to Bourdieu of Oct-Nov 1782 found none of 68, 36, 54, 23. A second witness is in the Shelburne papers at the Clements Library, vol. 35 no. 55 (HMC Fifth Report, 1876, p. 256: 'written partly in Cypher'), the volume of catalogue entry 772, which does not name this letter. All readings are the contributor's AI agents'. No maintainer has seen the images: digital.tcl.sc.edu did not answer on 20 Nov 2026 by script, in the app's browser or in Chrome. No reading is claimed; the lead is not vetted.
why: Henry Laurens, out of the Tower and in France, writes to a London friend about the Paris peace talks of summer 1782 with numbers for persons and causes; the seven numbers still open, and the numbers of his other letters to Bourdieu (4 June, 28 August, 30 November 1782), can be tested against his clear letters of the same days.
score_note: Scored by the maintainers at the integration of PR #827 (21 Nov 2026) from the contributor's research note (research/laurens_bourdieu_1782/) and the project's two reviews of it; the images were seen by the contributor's AI agents, not by the project. Solvability 2: 13 numbers in a clear letter, open only to parallel passages, and the edition finds the numbers not fixed to persons. Difficulty 4: 13 tokens allow no statistics.
verify: A maintainer opens image 2204 (page 2, lines 11 to 21: twelve numbers and the marked quotation), image 2497 (the postscript to Franklin, 7 Aug) and image 2460 (28 Aug: the passage with 45, 19, 68 and the address) and checks them against the two readings in research/laurens_bourdieu_1782/. Then: does Franklin's letter to Laurens of 19 Aug 1782 (Franklin Papers vol. 38) mention Bourdieu? Open Papers of Henry Laurens vol. 15 (pp. 526-528, 551-552, the index under Bourdieu) for an abstract of this letter. Ask the Clements Library for images of Shelburne papers vol. 35 no. 55 and see whether that witness keeps or expands the numbers. Search Lasry's papers and HistoCrypt.
